metadata.title: Irish General Election 2024 cross-party manifesto comparison
metadata.scope: Nine parties; six policy dimensions; 2024 election manifestos, not current party positions.
metadata.method: Original party manifestos were inspected directly where an accessible PDF was available. Page references are printed manifesto pages. Costings distinguish party-authored assumptions/estimates from the independent PBO tax-and-welfare microsimulation. PBO results cover seven parties and selected tax/welfare measures only; they do not independently cost full manifestos, public services, capital projects or infrastructure. Aontú and Independent Ireland were not included in the PBO model.
limitations: The first comparison is thematic, not page-by-page. Add exact page references and selected quotations before presenting individual proposals as fully verified.
Aontú link currently resolves to a policy portal, not a direct manifesto PDF.
Independent Ireland link is an archive index, not a direct party PDF.
Do not conflate 2024 manifestos with later party policy, alternative budgets or adopted Government policy.
Omission from a summary does not mean the party has no policy on the subject.
global_limitations: Page references are printed page numbers in the manifesto. Ranges marked approximate or requiring verification must not be cited as exact.
PBO microsimulation assesses selected tax and welfare measures using SWITCH and EVE; it does not assess public-service provision, health/education delivery, infrastructure or full capital programmes.
PBO results are modelled average disposable-income effects relative to its baseline, not forecasts of actual household outcomes and not a verdict on policy desirability.
Party-authored costings are reported as party estimates, not independent verification. Annual recurring costs must not be conflated with one-off capital costs or multi-year totals.
Manifesto commitments are historical 2024 proposals and are not current party positions or adopted Programme for Government measures.

checks.housing: The manifesto says capacity will rise to 60,000 homes per year by 2030. It also lists a €250m Modern Methods of Construction fund, a €2bn Towns Investment Fund and at least €3bn additional Irish Water investment. These are separate commitments and should not be summed as housing output.
checks.costing: The fiscal rule sets net spending growth to moderate from 6.6% in 2026 to 5.5% by 2030. It says departmental costings were carried out with relevant departments, Public Expenditure/NDP Delivery and Finance. The manifesto also identifies a €20bn reserve. These are party assumptions, not an independent audit.

costing.type: Party-published fiscal framework and departmental costing statement
key_figures: Net spending growth path: 6.6% in 2026, 6.0% in 2027 and 2028, 5.5% in 2029 and 2030
€20bn reserve stated for existing services and public-service pay
costing.independent_review: PBO tax/welfare microsimulation available; it does not assess housing, health, infrastructure or other public-service spending.

pbo.summary: PBO modelled tax and welfare measures; average disposable income changes were small across deciles. Poorest decile +0.1%; richest -0.4% versus the PBO baseline.
pbo.caveat: Not a full manifesto cost or macroeconomic forecast.
pbo.scope_note: PBO's report includes this party among seven parties modelled. It covers selected tax and welfare measures, not the full manifesto.

verification.evidence_quality: Official party PDF inspected; printed-page section references checked. Costing statements are party-provided and should not be described as independent verification.

checks.housing: The manifesto commits to 300,000 homes by 2030 and €40bn housing budget over five years, average €8bn annually. It also proposes 9,000 affordable purchase homes annually by 2030 and Help to Buy relief up to €40,000.
checks.costing: The manifesto has a dedicated costings section on printed page 116. It states €31.2bn total spending increase for 2026–2030 (including €26.4bn current and €4.8bn capital), €14.1bn extra capital expenditure from Apple receipts, €6bn tax revenue from wage growth and €1.1bn revenue-raising measures.

pbo.summary: PBO estimated average household disposable income falls in every decile under the modelled tax/welfare package; poorest decile -2.7%, richest -0.4%.
pbo.caveat: PBO's modelled tax/welfare package is not a full assessment of all manifesto spending or service proposals.

checks.housing: The manifesto proposes at least 50,000 homes annually, direct social housing build rising to 15,000 annually by 2028, and a long-term goal of social housing at 20% of stock. It says this requires an additional €2.8bn capital allocation per year by 2029, with about €1bn per year for affordable housing and cost-rental measures.
checks.costing: Appendix 'Budget Plans and Costings' begins on printed page 130. Labour asked the PBO to model an alternative annual expenditure ceiling of 6%; this is an expenditure framework and costing appendix, not a line-by-line independent costing of every manifesto promise.

checks.housing: The manifesto proposes 8,000 vacant-home grants up to €70,000 (stated party cost €560m/year), a €30,000 above-shop refurbishment grant (stated €60m), 15,000 social and affordable homes annually, and a no-fault eviction ban.
checks.costing: The party gives itemised estimates for several proposals: €560m/year for vacant-home grants, €60m for above-shop grants, €259m for 3,500 nurses/midwives, €195m/year for zero VAT on electricity, €764m/year for hospitality VAT reduction (up to), and €45m set-up plus €15m annual running cost for an efficiency department. These are party estimates, not independent costings. No PBO microsimulation result was located for Aontú.

checks.housing: The manifesto proposes an additional €600m per year for infrastructure supporting community/social housing, tax incentives for vacant-property development and tax-free rents below €1,000. Its costing section gives a €45m set-up cost and €15m annual operating budget for a Department of Efficiency and Reform, with a stated goal of 10% savings of 2024 government spend over the next government.
checks.costing: The manifesto has a dedicated costings page (printed page 25) and links some measures to it. The 10% savings figure is a goal, not an independently verified saving or a full consolidated fiscal balance. PBO did not include Independent Ireland in its six-party model.
